expectations.text: Recommends scalar quantization as starting point
expectations.evidence: Section titled 'Scalar quantization (int8) - recommended starting point' and the recommendation section states: 'Start with scalar quantization. It is safe, predictable, and gives you 4x reduction.'

expectations.text: Mentions binary quantization is compatible with OpenAI models
expectations.evidence: States: 'Your model (text-embedding-3-small) is compatible with binary quantization' and 'OpenAI embeddings work well with binary quantization.'

States: 'Requires oversampling (3-5x) and rescoring to maintain good recall. Without rescoring, expect significant accuracy degradation.' Also: 'Make sure to enable oversampling (set to 3-5x) and rescoring against full-precision vectors. This gives 32x compression with 95%+ recall when rescoring is enabled.'

Provides formula: '80M * 1536 * 4 bytes (float32) = ~491 GB just for raw vectors' and per-quantization estimates: '~123 GB for quantized vectors' (scalar) and '~15 GB for quantized vectors' (binary). Note: the formula does not include HNSW overhead multiplier (only raw vector size), but it does provide concrete memory estimates.

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend product quantization as first choice
expectations.evidence: Product quantization is mentioned as a 'configurable middle ground' option but is clearly listed third, after scalar and binary. The recommendation section explicitly states 'Start with scalar quantization' as step 1 and binary as step 2. Product quantization is not recommended as a first choice.
